name: Water course security
short_description: Build rope fencing around water course
description: Fencing to avoid contact with water course.  Building new 2 rope fence. Assuming same costs per meter as in secure_fencing = 11 kr/m. Also, establishment of water throughs on pasture with water from barn. Assumptions: 200 cows herd, 1000m fence  300 meter distance from main water source, daily water intake per cow: 60L, reinforced area around troughs, installation and materials. Water supplpy and pumpsystem = 55.000(Water supply and pump = 20.000 kr, 300 m pipeline = 20.000 kr, work = 15.000), water troughs, 4 stations = 25.000 kr, reinforced area (gravel layer) around troughs 30 m2 each = 50.000 kr, installation and tehnical costs = 30.000. Total = 160.000 kr + 1000 m fencing
label: investment_capacity
comment: You should maybe also add a variable cost for extra the water supply needed during the six months grazing - instead of cows drinking from a natural water source. A cow consumption of 60 L/d means 60*120*200 = 1.440 m3 per grazing season. The Danish price is ~8 kr. pr. m3 + fixed charges (up to 70 kr./m3). However, if water is used for animal drinking, the farmer can get a substantial reduction in the waterwaste charge. THIS IS NOT YET INCLUDED...

name: Water course security
description: Not able to use low-land for grazing youngstock implies extra feed costs and workload. Feed cost, youngstock = 7.30 kr/d, other costs (straw etc) 1.09 kr./d,  workload = 9h/heifer year = 1.5 minute/d.  Assuming 120 grazing days, youngstock grazing in the age 6-24 months.  Period 6-24 months = 0.75 calf year - 120 days of grazing = 0.25 year. 1.1 calf per cow year. *** By Phil: Daily costs (kr/day) and labor (min/day) are converted to annual per cow-year values by multiplying by 365 days and the combined exposure factor (0.75 × 0.25 × 1.1), reflecting time in age group, grazing period, and calves per cow-year.
label: mixed_variable_labor
comment: I have prioritised youngstock here as they are most likely to be grazed on low-lands. An alternative could be to have scenario where cows cannot go to pasture - or a fourth scenario where both groups has to be housed
